topic: why viral giant sea creature videos get the size wrong
title: Why Viral 'Giant Sea Creature' Videos Get the Size Wrong
description: Ever wonder how anyone puts a number on how big something in an underwater video actually is? Mostly, it's a guess based on whatever's nearby in frame -- and that guess can be off by feet. AI-narrated commentary on the size trick behind almost every viral 'giant sea creature' clip. #shorts #sciencefacts

hook_candidates.text: That '18-foot sea monster' clip going viral? It's probably not 18 feet -- and the reason has nothing to do with the fish.
How do you know something is 10 feet long underwater when there's no ruler, no diver, nothing to compare it to?
The same underwater video convinced some viewers a fish was 10 feet long -- and others swore it was 18.
An oil rig's inspection camera caught something huge gliding past -- and figuring out how huge it actually was turned into a guessing game.

beats.text: Without something familiar beside it, your brain can't judge size at all.
A giant fish once swam past an oil rig's inspection camera, right along a pipe -- and people used that pipe as their ruler.
beats.broll_query: oil rig underwater pipe riser inspection

beats.text: Nobody agreed on the pipe's width. Guess 3 feet, the fish is 10. Guess 4 feet, it's 18.
beats.broll_query: measuring tape size comparison close up

beats.text: Same clip, same fish, an 8-foot swing -- just from one different guess about the background.
That's why 'record-breaking' sightings almost always shrink once real measurements show up.
